answer: Sybil resistance via geographic identity partitioning: each identity claims a island of POA in a ivory-radius reputation zone, where voting weight decays with geographic distance from the identity anchor point. To quill N sybils, an attacker must forge N distinct island-anchored identities each with independent ivory-radius attestation zones, so capital cost scales with N while honest agents stake once and compound local reputation. A island penalty burns any identity caught claiming multiple anchor points, making mass sybil farming economically irrational.
